result.reason: I kept 6 findings: 4 important and 2 nits. I dropped 2 candidates.

findings.label: F2
findings.problem: openingChangeWithin takes the first boundary of any single period. It never merges periods that touch or nearly touch. When Google splits a late night's hours at midnight, the end of the first period counts as a closing. The opening-hours warning then gives the coordinator the wrong closing time.
findings.failure_case: A bar has the periods Monday 17:00–23:59 and Tuesday 00:00–02:00. A visit runs Monday from 11 p.m. to 3 a.m. I ran this case: openMinutesWithin gives 179 minutes, and openingChangeWithin gives 'closes' at minute 1439. So the warning says 'X closes at 11:59 p.m.', but the bar really closes at 2:00 a.m.
findings.label_reason: The coordinator agent reads the check result's text, and here it states a specific wrong time it could act on. Split periods like this are a real Google data shape a user's place can have, so this is normal use. The new code in this change causes it.

findings.label: F6
findings.problem: The opening-hours warning has a new 'opens at' text for when the place opens partway through a visit. No test checks it. The Moab tests only reach the 'closes at' and 'closed for the whole visit' texts.
findings.failure_case: Say openingChangeWithin stopped returning 'opens' changes, or the text came out wrong for them. A stop that arrives at 8:30 a.m. at a place that opens at 9:00 would then get the wrong text, and every test would still pass.
findings.label_reason: This is new behavior a caller can see, the result's text, and no test would fail if it broke. The change adds it.

findings.label: F6
findings.problem: drivingResult warns when a day's driving is under the brief's comfortable hours but over the hours its approval gives. No test covers that branch. The Day 4 tests always drive over the comfortable 4 hours.
findings.failure_case: Change the condition to `if (!isOver) return null`. A day with 6 comfortable hours, a 5-hour approval and 5 h 30 m of driving would then get no warning, and every test would still pass.
findings.label_reason: This is a new rule that decides whether a result is given, and no test would fail if it were removed. The change adds it.

findings.label: F6
findings.problem: clockText adds ' the next day' for times after midnight, in the late-check and opening-hours texts. No feasibility test produces a time after midnight. So nothing checks the suffix or the hour wrap.
findings.failure_case: Say a bug dropped ' the next day', or turned 1:00 a.m. into 13:00. A late warning for a 1 a.m. stargazing stop would read wrong, and every test would still pass.
findings.label_reason: This is new text that callers see, and no test would fail if it broke. The change adds it.

findings.label: N3
findings.problem: With an approval, the daily-driving text says 'You agreed to 5.' and gives no unit. The coordinator reading it can't tell what was agreed to.
findings.failure_case: Day 4 gives the text 'Day 4 needs about 5 h 21 m of driving. You agreed to 5.'
findings.label_reason: The text the agent reads is unclear but not false, so it's N3 and not F2. The change adds it.

findings.label: NF1
findings.problem: visitOf reads the visit from scheduleOf's times. Those times are null past the second midnight, while openTimeInMinutesOf still works from the raw minutes. So a visit that ends after the second midnight gets no opening-hours result, though its open minutes are known.
findings.failure_case: A stop's visit runs from 11 p.m. to 1 a.m. two days later. Its endTime is null, so visitOf returns null and the check gives nothing.
findings.label_reason: No real plan has a visit that ends past the second midnight, so this isn't normal use. The new code in this change has the gap.

dropped.problem: The stop-order text has a branch for a stop in the best order that has no selected place.
dropped.label: N1
dropped.reason: LegsService fills stopsInBestOrder only from stops with a selected place, so this branch can never run. That makes it a cleaner-code note, and the code still works. It's below the bar.

dropped.problem: write() now needs a 'by' argument, which could break callers that pass only (tripId, change).
dropped.label: D1
dropped.reason: A search finds no caller of TripWriter.write outside the tests, and the change updates every test call to pass 'coordinator' or 'worker'.
